items.title: [R9][Q1] Independent support-two reconstruction and production-resource audit
items.body:
## Objective

Move ORION-Q1 from a sharp scoped theorem to a journal-grade independently auditable result without diluting or conflating it with the combined AB paper.

The frozen mathematical claim is the support-two theorem for the declared shared-Tag TARE compiler and its exact objective/scope. The issue must terminate separately on theorem correctness and on production-resource interpretation.

## Expert lanes

### Lane Q1-A — algebraic proof reconstruction

Background: quantum compilation, Pauli algebra, exact synthesis, and additive/combinatorial normal forms.

Tasks:

1. Reconstruct the theorem from definitions without importing the manuscript proof text.
2. Enumerate every quantifier, feasibility premise, objective premise, shared-Tag assumption, and exclusion.
3. Produce either a proof dependency graph or the first minimal counterexample.
4. Check all boundary supports 0, 1, 2, and 3, including degenerate generators and shared auxiliary cases.
5. Distinguish existence of a support-two optimum from uniqueness, algorithmic discoverability, and production cost.

Required terminals: `PROOF_RECONSTRUCTED`, `COUNTEREXAMPLE`, `SCOPE_MISMATCH`, `DEFINITION_AMBIGUITY`, `CANNOT_CHECK`.

### Lane Q1-B — structurally independent finite attack

Background: exact finite search, SAT/SMT/ILP, symmetry reduction, and proof-producing enumeration.

Tasks:

1. Encode the smallest nontrivial frozen Q1 instances independently of the registered implementation.
2. Search exhaustively for an optimum requiring support at least three.
3. Include positive support-two witnesses, support-one nonexamples, objective-tie cases, and intentionally broken shared-Tag controls.
4. Preserve source manifests, symmetry actions, solver certificates, negative controls, and all disagreements.

Required terminals: `NO_SUPPORT3_COUNTEREXAMPLE_IN_DECLARED_DOMAIN`, `SUPPORT3_COUNTEREXAMPLE`, `ENCODING_DISAGREEMENT`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `CANNOT_CHECK`.

A bounded PASS corroborates the encoding only; it does not prove the all-size theorem.

### Lane Q1-C — production-resource map

Background: fault-tolerant quantum resource estimation, Clifford+T/TARE compilation, circuit semantics, and architecture-aware cost models.

For each abstract support unit, define and verify the exact production object it counts. The map must state:

- circuit or grammar object;
- allowed fusion/cancellation/reconstruction moves;
- ancilla assumptions;
- measurement/feed-forward assumptions;
- connectivity and parallelism assumptions;
- whether the resource is T count, T depth, non-Clifford support, qubit support, search support, or another quantity;
- conversion theorem or explicit statement that no conversion theorem is known.

Produce two columns for every headline statement:

1. theorem-owned abstract support claim;
2. production-resource consequence, with all additional premises.

Required terminals: `FAITHFUL_RESOURCE_MAP`, `PARTIAL_RESOURCE_MAP`, `NO_FAITHFUL_MAP`, `PRODUCTION_COUNTEREXAMPLE`, `CANNOT_CHECK`.

### Lane Q1-D — independent quantum reviewer

The reviewer must be institutionally or procedurally independent of the original proof construction. They receive the frozen definitions, claim ledger, proof, and attack receipts. They must report major/minor errors, nearest-work overlap, missing physical assumptions, and whether the production interpretation is proportionate.

Required terminals: `CLEAR`, `REVISION_REQUIRED`, `REJECT_THEOREM`, `REJECT_PRODUCTION_INTERPRETATION`, `CANNOT_CHECK`.

## Promotion gate

Q1 may be called journal-submission grade only when all of the following are present:

- exact theorem reconstruction or an independently checkable proof audit;
- no unresolved support-three counterexample in the declared finite attack domain;
- a complete claim ledger with frozen scope;
- a faithful or explicitly partial production-resource map;
- nearest-work and novelty audit using current primary sources;
- independent quantum reviewer report;
- source/result/environment manifests and negative controls.

No finite search, internal review, CI PASS, or manuscript polish alone grants journal authority.

## Codex handoff

Codex should create separate branches for Q1-A/Q1-B/Q1-C, avoiding the protected Task-3 implementation branch and avoiding reuse of AB's complete-fusion assumptions. Any counterexample, mapping failure, or definition ambiguity is a successful harness terminal and must remain visible.
